India could benefit over the long term as businesses and public services adopt artificial intelligence more widely, while its equities could help investors weather near-term volatility in AI stocks, Deutsche Bank said.

The report highlighted a reversal in foreign investment, with overseas investors buying a record $9.5 billion of Indian equities in November after $26 billion in net sales over the first nine months of 2026.

India’s stock market is dominated by banks, healthcare and IT services, and as of 17 November the Nifty IT Index’s one-year correlation with the Nasdaq Composite was close to zero, according to Bloomberg data.

The bank’s longer-term case for the economy rests on a young population and established digital infrastructure that could make widely available AI tools cheaper to deploy at scale.

Lending illustrates the opportunity, with digital identity and instant payments already in place and AI offering lenders a way to assess borrowers who lack a conventional credit history.

The same technology could automate routine outsourcing tasks such as customer support and junior coding, though Deutsche Bank considers fears of widespread disruption overdone.

India’s technology services firms already adapt global tools for corporate clients, giving them scope, in the bank’s view, to use AI to improve higher-value work such as software development and analytics.

The report cautioned that broader productivity gains would depend on companies redesigning how they work, while delays in expanding the power grid could hold back data centre growth.

For investors, the hedge could lose some of its appeal if sentiment towards AI stocks recovers and stays positive, the bank added.
